MOSAIC: Multi-customer Orchestration System for Adaptive Intake and Continuous Delivery. A provider-neutral system for preparing governed solution definitions.
SME: Subject matter expert. A specialist who evaluates the business and technical proposal with the customer; expertise alone does not confer decision authority.
AI: Artificial intelligence. Here, software that helps interpret requests and prepare draft analysis; it does not approve customer decisions.
API: Application programming interface. A defined way for software systems to exchange requests and results.
APIs: Application programming interfaces: defined connections between software systems.
MCP: Model Context Protocol. A standard interface through which an agent can call tools and retrieve permitted context.
CLI: Command-line interface. A program operated through typed commands.
HTML: Hypertext Markup Language. The format used for these browser-readable reports.
JSON: JavaScript Object Notation. A structured format used for evidence, validation and workflow records.
SHA-256: Secure Hash Algorithm with a 256-bit digest. A content fingerprint that changes when source bytes change; it is not a signature or approval.
SHA: Secure Hash Algorithm. A family of content-fingerprint algorithms.
ID: Identifier. A stable label used to cross-reference a record.
IDs: Identifiers. Stable labels used to cross-reference records.
SYN: Synthetic initiative identifier. It denotes fictional demonstration data, not a live customer record.
RUN: Workflow run identifier. It binds the recorded request and package content; it is not approval.
EVD: Evidence identifier. A reference to a source allowed by the active source policy.
REQ: Requirement identifier. A traceable statement of what the solution must satisfy.
UNK: Unknown identifier. An unanswered question that may block a decision.
RSK: Risk identifier. A recorded potential adverse outcome.
GAP: Gap identifier. Missing information or capability requiring attention.
ASM: Assumption identifier. An unverified premise used in analysis.
CLM: Claim identifier. A statement labeled by its evidence or decision status.
DEP: Dependency identifier. Something the proposal relies on.
OPT: Option identifier. One of the contrasting solution alternatives.
DOS: Dossier coverage identifier. A design-documentation area, not a completion score.
PLAN: Readiness-plan identifier. A proposed plan with explicit requirements and missing evidence.
SLA: Service-level agreement. An agreed service or freshness target; no agreement is inferred here.
SLAs: Service-level agreements. Explicit commitments that require authorized owners.
SLO: Service-level objective. A proposed measurable reliability or service target.
SBOM: Software bill of materials. An inventory of software components and dependencies; no completed inventory is claimed here.
PR: Pull request. A revision-control review mechanism; it is not implicit customer authorization.
PRs: Pull requests. Proposed changes submitted for review in revision control.
IT: Information technology. The people and systems responsible for organizational technology.
HR: Human resources. The organizational function responsible for workforce matters.
UTC: Coordinated Universal Time. A common time reference independent of local daylight-saving changes.
min: Minutes. Here this is an allocation within the proposed meeting agenda, not a delivery schedule.
PDF: Portable Document Format. A fixed-layout document format.
PDFs: Portable Document Format files. Fixed-layout documents that still need version and ownership controls.
RAI: Responsible artificial intelligence. Controls for accountable, safe and transparent use of AI.
NIST: National Institute of Standards and Technology. Its publications may inform customer-specific alignment targets, not automatic compliance.
SOC 2: System and Organization Controls 2. An assurance framework; this draft does not establish certification or compliance.
ITIL 4: Information Technology Infrastructure Library, version 4. Service-management guidance; alignment must be assessed for the customer.
N/A: Not applicable or not recorded in the source table; inspect the surrounding context before interpreting it.
RBAC: Role-based access control. Permissions assigned according to authorized roles.
SSO: Single sign-on. A way to access multiple services through an established identity session.
PII: Personally identifiable information. Information that can identify an individual.
RAG: Retrieval-augmented generation. A pattern that supplies retrieved source material to a model; retrieval alone does not guarantee accurate answers.
CI: Continuous integration. Automated checks applied to proposed software changes.
CD: Continuous delivery. Preparing changes for release; actual release still requires the applicable authorization.
IaC: Infrastructure as code. Machine-readable infrastructure definitions; execution is outside this discussion draft.
UI: User interface. The controls and information a person interacts with.
UX: User experience. How effectively and comfortably a person can complete their work.
URL: Uniform Resource Locator. The address of a resource.
URLs: Uniform Resource Locators. Resource addresses, not proof of access or authority.
HTTP: Hypertext Transfer Protocol. A protocol for exchanging web requests and responses.
HTTPS: HTTP over an encrypted TLS connection.
TLS: Transport Layer Security. Encryption and authentication for network connections.
TCO: Total cost of ownership. Delivery, operation, maintenance and change costs over a stated period.
ROI: Return on investment. Benefits relative to costs; no measured return is claimed by this report.
FTE: Full-time equivalent. A unit of labor capacity, not necessarily a reduction in headcount.
PoC: Proof of concept. A bounded test of feasibility, not production approval.
MVP: Minimum viable product. A narrowly scoped usable release; the scope requires customer agreement.
SQL: Structured Query Language. A language used to query and manage relational data.
SSRF: Server-side request forgery. A risk where untrusted input causes a server to access unintended destinations.
XSS: Cross-site scripting. A risk where untrusted text is treated as executable browser content.
PUBLIC-SUMMARY: Source-policy classification for a summary of public information. It does not verify customer statements or authorize live source access.
SYNTHETIC: Fictional demonstration information. It must not be presented as an actual customer record.
